olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $S$ has $2002$ elements. For $0\leq N\leq 2^{2002}$, prove every subset of $S$ can be colored black or white so that (a) any two white subsets have white union; (b) any two black subsets have black union; (c) exactly $N$ subsets are white.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2002

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $\triangle ABC$ satisfy $\cot^2\frac{A}{2}+2\cot^2\frac{B}{2}+3\cot^2\frac{C}{2}=\frac{36s^2}{7r^2}$, where $s,r$ are semiperimeter and inradius. Prove $\triangle ABC$ is similar to an integer-sided triangle with no common divisors and find those integers.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2002

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Prove any monic polynomial of degree $n$ with real coefficients is the average of two monic polynomials of degree $n$ with $n$ real roots each.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2002

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $a,b>2$ be integers. Prove there exist positive integers $n_1,\ldots,n_k$ with $n_1=a$, $n_k=b$, and $n_in_{i+1}\mid n_i+n_{i+1}$ for each $i$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2002

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: From an $n\times n$ stamp sheet, tear out blocks of 3 consecutive stamps in a row or column. Let $b(n)$ = minimum blocks to make further tearing impossible. Prove $\frac{1}{7}n^2-cn\leq b(n)\leq\frac{1}{5}n^2+dn$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2002
